scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

The person in question is a woman who had a conversation with her mom. There were a couple of incidents where she told her mom that her parenting was bad. The first time was when her mom was talking about not believing in doctors and not taking her siblings to the doctor even when they begged her. The woman told her mom that this wasn't okay and that it almost cost her her life because she was hospitalized and on bedrest for months. She warned her mom that if she keeps doing this, one of them might die. Her mom didn't take it well but eventually brushed it off.

Then, later, her mom asked her to get her a drink and said, "you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years." The woman responded that she doesn't know because her grandparents raised her and she still doesn't know anything about her mom. Her mom got upset, cried, and accused her of being mean and trying to make her seem like a bad person. The woman explained she wasn't trying to be mean but was just saying it's not cool to not take kids to the doctor and that she didn't grow up with her mom, so she doesn't know her.

A few weeks later, they went out again. The woman had bought her brother a phone because their family was taking his phone, which another family member pays for. She made it clear that this new phone was strictly for her brother. However, she found out that her mom was taking and using this phone too. When she confronted her mom, she told her she didn't want to take the phone back because she didn't want her brother to be punished, but she would if her mom didn't stop stealing it. She also mentioned that her mom was keeping all her brother's work money, which was already bad, and not to touch the phone. Her mom got upset, started yelling and crying, saying she shouldn't be treated like a bad mother. The woman told her mom she kind of is one. Her mom had a meltdown, said she doesn't need her in her life, and left.

Now, the family is saying she shouldn't have treated her mom like that, even if her mom wasn't great to her. The question is, AITA (Am I the Asshole)?

Alright, so I need to evaluate whether the woman's actions were morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down.

First, the woman's mom has a history of not taking her kids to the doctor, which the woman says almost cost her life. That's a serious issue. The woman confronted her mom about this, which seems justified because it's a matter of health and safety. However, the way she did it might have been harsh. She told her mom that she's a bad mother, which could be seen as mean, but it's also a truthful statement based on her experiences.

In the second incident, the mom made a comment about the woman knowing what she likes because she's raised her for 26 years. The woman responded by pointing out that her grandparents raised her, so she doesn't know her mom. This seems like a factual statement, but it could be hurtful because it's pointing out the mom's absence in her life.

The third incident involves the phone. The woman bought her brother a phone to prevent it from being taken by others. When she found out her mom was using it, she confronted her, which is reasonable because it's her money and the phone is for her brother. However, she told her mom she kind of is a bad mother, which again is a harsh statement but based on past experiences.

Now, considering the family's reaction, they think she shouldn't have treated her mom like that. But from the woman's perspective, she's standing up for herself and her siblings' well-being. She's addressing behaviors that have caused harm, which is a form of self-protection and advocacy.

On the other hand, calling her mom a bad mother directly could be seen as mean, but it's also a truthful assessment based on her experiences. It's a tough line because while it's justified, it's also hurtful and could damage their relationship further.

I think the key here is whether the woman's actions were necessary to protect herself and her siblings, even if they were hurtful. She's addressing harmful behavior, which is a moral obligation, but the way she did it might not be the most compassionate approach. However, given the context of her mom's past actions, it's understandable why she would feel the need to confront her.

So, considering all this, I would lean towards the action being morally acceptable because she's standing up for her and her siblings' well-being, even though the method was harsh. It's a tough call, but I think the intent was to protect rather than to be mean.
